title: Write the Vision
backstory: Habakkuk had asked God why He would hold His tongue while the wicked devoured people more righteous than themselves (Habakkuk 1:13). So the prophet climbs up like a sentry going on duty, saying he will stand upon his watch and set himself upon the tower until he sees what the LORD will say to him (Habakkuk 2:1). The reply comes with an order to write the vision plain enough for a runner to read, and at its heart sits one short line — the just shall live by his faith (Habakkuk 2:2-4) — that Paul would take up again in his letter to Rome (Romans 1:17).

passages.synopsis: Habakkuk stood at his watch like a guard on a tower, waiting to see what God would say. The LORD answered and told him to write the vision plainly on tablets, so plainly that a runner could read it. The vision was for an appointed time, and even if it seemed slow, it would surely come. Then came the great promise: the proud heart is not right, but the just shall live by his faith.

God said that proud Babylon, always grabbing for more, would never be satisfied. One day all the nations it had robbed would take up a taunting song against it. Woe to him who piles up what is not his, for suddenly the tables would turn. Because Babylon had spoiled many nations, the remnant of the peoples would spoil Babylon.

More woes fell on the proud empire. Woe to those who build their house by taking from others, thinking a high nest will keep them safe. Woe to those who build a town with blood, for even the stones in the wall would cry out against them. All that grasping labor ends in smoke, but the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.

The last woes fall on the violent and on those who trust in idols. All the harm Babylon had done to the land and the city would come rolling back to cover it. What good is a carved image, a teacher of lies covered over with gold and silver, with no breath in it at all? An idol cannot wake up, speak, or help anyone who calls to it. But the LORD is in His holy temple, so let all the earth keep silence before Him.

triviaQuestions.question: What did the LORD tell Habakkuk to do with the vision?
options: Write it and make it plain upon tables
Seal it up until the last day
triviaQuestions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:2 — "And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it."

triviaQuestions.question: According to the vision, how shall the just live?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:4 — "Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith."

triviaQuestions.question: With what shall the earth be filled, as the waters cover the sea?
options: The knowledge of the glory of the LORD
triviaQuestions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:14 — "For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea."

triviaQuestions.question: Where is the LORD while all the earth keeps silence?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:20 — "But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him."

The just shall live by his...

reflection: God told Habakkuk the answer would surely come, even if it seemed slow. What promise of God are you waiting for, and how can you keep trusting Him while you wait?
